The learned Advocate appearing for the writ petitioner submits that as the application dated 27.01.04 filed by the Judgment-debtor or under Order 26, rule II of the Code of Civil Procedure has not been disposed of and in the mean-time the possession of the mortgaged property, which is now under possession of the Judgment-debtor, ordered to be delivered to the Decree-holder bank and that the Judgment debtor will be put to suffer irreparable injury if possession, as ordered for, is delivered inasmuch_ as the said property is the only homestead land of the writ petitioner and that subsequent to the passing of the decree, the judgment-debtor, on the passing of the decree, the Judgment debtor. on the assurance of the Decree-holder bank, has already deposited the cost of the suit plus 10% of the claimed amount with the Decree-holder Bank to get remission of the interest and that prayer is pending and that this fact has not been considered by the Court below and that the said amount as deposited, has not also been adjusted with the decretal amount and hence the judgment-debtor being aggrieved moved this application under Article 102 of the Constitution. 

 5. It appears that the Judgment debtor wants adjustment of the aforesaid amount which they have deposited after passing of the decree, on the assurance of the Decree-holder bank to the effect that the interest amount will be remitted and that the said matter is still rending and is under consideration of the Bank. We are of the view that the executing Court can not look 

 beyond the decree and if the claim of the Judgment debtor writ petitioner is correct that it had deposited certain amount passing of the decree it must be adjusted with the decretal amount and further the assurance given by the Decree-holder Bank, as submitted, being pending matter ; can be decided by the bank at any point of time but prior to sale of the mortgaged property and that the Decree-holder hank can satisfy its decree by adjustment of the amount deposited and the remission of interest.
